texts.facts: As a result, the rider of the said motor cycle lost control and hit the said Bolero. Due to the sudden impact, the claimant fell down and sustained injuries all over his body. Due to the injuries sustained and disability suffered, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation. 3.1 On service of notice, respondent No.1 was placed ex parte. Respondent No.2 filed written statement denying the claim of the claimant including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. Bolero vehicle.
texts.arguments: Per contra, learned counsel representing the insurance company contends that there is no error, illegality or perversity in the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal. Due to the accident, the claimant suffered permanent disability and he would not be able to sit, squat to perform his regular day to day activities of earning as opined by the doctor.

7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the material on record, it is seen that FIR NC: 2024:KHC:16244 has been registered against driver of the offending vehicle i.e, Bolero for the offences punishable under Secti

The occurrence of accident, involvement of vehicle, injuries sustained by the claimant and the accident occurred due to negligence of driver of the offending vehicle are established by the evidence adduced and the documents produced as per
Therefore, the tribunal rightly attributed the negligence against driver of the Bolero vehicle.

8. Now coming to the question of age, avocation, income and disability suffered by the claimant, it is seen that the claimant was aged 33 years as on the date of accident and the appropriate multiplier would be '16', which is rightly appli
Though the claimant pleaded that he was working as a weaver earning Rs.15,000/- per month, no material is placed before the Court with regard to the same and proof of income.

In the absence of the NC: 2024:KHC:16244 same, the Tribunal has taken the income of the claimant to be Rs.7,000/-
per month, whereas the Legal Services Authority chart prescribes the notional income of Rs.9,500/-
per month for the accident
Accordingly, the same is taken as income for computation in the present case as against Rs.7,000/- taken by the Tribunal.
9. The doctor has been examined as PW.2.
He opined disability to an extent of 64.14% to right lower limb and 32% to whole body.
The Tribunal taken the whole body disability to be 18%.
I am in agreement with learned counsel for the appellant that the disability assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

There is no contra material placed on record and cogent evidence adduced by the Insurance Company by producing second opinion or any other medical opinion to contradict the statement of the doctor/PW.2.
Even one-third portion of particular limb disability is taken as a whole body disability, it would come to 21%.

10. I am in agreement with learned counsel for the claimant that considering the fact that there is a disability of 64% to the right lower limb and 32% to whole body, future prospects requires to be awarded in this case.

Considering the disability suffered by the claimant, this Court deems it appropriate to add 40% of income towards future prospects while computing compensation under the head of loss of future earnings.
11. In view of the above, loss of future earnings would be Rs.5,36,256/- {[Rs.9,500 + 3800 (40%)] x 12 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:16244 x 16 x 21%} as against Rs.2,41,920/- awarded by the Tribunal.
12. The tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award additional amount of Rs.20,000/-.
In all, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.

13. The tribunal awarded Rs.8,000/- towards food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges, which does not call for interference and the same is retained.
14.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.33,500/- towards medical expenses on the basis of the actual bills produced by the claimant, which does not call for interference.
15. The Tribunal awarded Rs.21,000/- towards loss of income during the period of treatment, which is on the lower side.
Considering the magnitude of injuries suffered by the claimant, atleast three months is required to recuperate and get back to normal day to day activities.

In view of this Court enhancing the income to Rs.9,500/-
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:16244 per month, Rs.28,500/- (Rs.9,500/- x 3) is awarded under this head.
16. The tribunal awarded Rs.35,000/- towards loss of amenities.
However, this Court deems it appropriate to award additional amount of Rs.10,000/-.
In all, Rs.45,000/- is awarded under this head.
The tribunal awarded Rs.25,000/- towards future medical expenses, which does not call for interference and the same is retained.

Coming to the question of Tribunal fixing 20% contributory negligence against the claimant, it is to be borne in mind that the claimant was not the rider of the motorcycle, but he was the pillion rider.
The finding arrived at by the Tribunal is not acceptable and same is erroneous and liable to be set aside.

Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the rider of a two wheeler, not to carry more than one person on the motorcycle and Section 194-C prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motorcycle rid
The fact that the claimant was a pillion rider on a motorcycle alongwith the rider and one more person is not in dispute.

The triple riding of the motorcycle by the rider without wearing of helmets may be violation of law,

In the present case, there is no cogent evidence of filing FIR or criminal prosecution against rider of the motorcycle.
Considering all these aspects, fastening 20% contributory negligence against claimant is perverse and same is set aside and the entire negligence is saddled on the driver of the Bolero vehicle.
As the policy was in force as on the date of occurrence of the accident, the 2nd respondent/insurer shall deposit the entire compensation.

20. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part;
ii) The impugned Judgment & Award dated 8th November 2019 passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.6325/2016, is modified.
iii) The appellant/claimant would be entitled
However, future medical expenses shall not carry interest.
vi) The enhanced compensation alongwith interest at 6% per annum shall be deposited by the respondent no.2/insurer within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
vii) The compensation amount shall be released in favour of the appellant-claimant as per the terms of the tribunal upon proper identification.
viii) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the tribunal shall stand intact.
ix) Registry is directed to transmit the original records, if any to the jurisdictional Tribunal forthwith.
